_comment: Databricks job: geocode new NAV customers, then run the daily dbt build.
Import with:
databricks jobs create --json @scripts/databricks/geocode_job.json
WHY ONE JOB WITH TWO TASKS rather than two scheduled jobs: the dbt build
reads ust_external.nav_customer_geocode. If geocoding ran on its own
schedule there would be a window where a new customer exists in
navrep.customer but has no coordinate, and int_rep_customer_presence would
silently report scenario 'unknown' for every visit to them. depends_on
removes that window.
WHY IT IS SAFE TO RUN DAILY: the script is incremental on address_hash, so
a day with no new customers sends zero requests and costs nothing. A day
with five new customers costs about 3 cents.
BEFORE FIRST RUN, create the secret (the Google key is third-party, so
unlike Databricks auth it cannot be ambient):
databricks secrets create-scope ust
databricks secrets put-secret ust google_geocoding_api_key
Databricks auth itself needs NO secret here: the run_as identity
authenticates ambiently via SparkSession. Give it read on navrep and
write on ust_external.
--limit 500 is a DELIBERATE BLAST-RADIUS CAP, not a performance setting. If
an upstream change ever rewrites every address, address_hash changes for
all 7,198 rows and an uncapped run would spend ~$36 unattended. With the
cap the damage is ~$2.50 and the backlog drains over subsequent days.
Remove it for a deliberate one-off backfill, run attended.
name: ust_daily_geocode_and_dbt

tasks.description: Geocode NAV customers whose address is new or changed. No-op on a quiet day.
Daily dbt build. Runs AFTER geocoding so new customers already have coordinates.

_task_environment_note: Set this on the geocode task in the job UI (Task > Advanced > Environment
variables), or via the API field below. The value is a secret REFERENCE:
Databricks resolves it at runtime and redacts it from logs, so the key
never appears in the job definition, the repo, or output.
